anomalies.observed: PCA9685PW pin 1 (A0) is on net +3.3V, the same net as VDD (pin 28). Every other address pin (A1 pin 2, A2 pin 3, A3 pin 4, A4 pin 5, A5 pin 24) is on GND.
anomalies.expected: With A0 tied high the PCA9685 responds at 0x41, not the specified 0x40. A0 should be tied to GND like the other address pins.

evidence.quote: PWM/servo driver | FCCPeripherals | NXP PCA9685PW (I2C 16-ch PWM), I2C addr 0x40

anomalies.impact: The PWM driver will not respond at the firmware's expected 0x40 address, so servo/PWM outputs will not be driven unless the software is changed to 0x41.

anomalies.observed: The LDO output (REG3 OUT) and the sensors/EEPROMs sit on net +3.3V, while the FCC decoupling capacitors and FCC pull-ups sit on a separate net +3V3 that has no regulator output connected to it.
anomalies.expected: A single regulated 3V3 rail should feed both the FCC and NAVC MCUs and all their decoupling, as the specification states that 3V3 feeds both MCUs and all I2C sensors.

evidence.quote: 3V3 feeds both MCUs (FCC, NAVC) and all I2C sensor ICs

anomalies.impact: If the two nets are truly separate, the FCC and NAVC MCU supply and their decoupling are not fed from the LDO, so those parts cannot power up. This may be a labelling quirk of the reference design rather than a tampering.

parsed.summary: The strongest deviation is PCA9685 address pin A0 tied to +3.3V instead of GND, which shifts the driver from the specified 0x40 to 0x41. A weaker concern is that the +3V3 and +3.3V rails are separate nets with only one regulator source.
